violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: chicken broth at 51F, unsalted butter at 54F in 2 DR UPR glass refrigerator. (56F).
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC discarded unsalted butter and chicken broth that had been in the refrigerator for more than four hours, and relocated all TCS foods that had been in the cooler for less than four hours.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: 2 DR UPR glass refrigerator at 56F.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC scheduled repair with technician during inspection. PIC will discontinued use of unite until the repair is completed.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: Observed no date marking for cooked black beans , tomato sauce, Alfredo sauce and etc. in 2 DR UPR Pepsi refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC understands all cooked/prepared foods kept for more than 24 hours must be date marked. PIC has date marked the aforementioned food items accordingly.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: bulk containers of rices and beans.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO LABEL ALL BULK CONTAINERS WITH THE LABEL ON THE OUTSIDE OF THE CONTAINER. PLEASE MAKE THIS CORRECTION BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed multiple sacks of potatoes being stored directly on the floor of the walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PIC MOVED THE SACKS OF POTATOES TO A NEARBY SHELVING UNIT.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed cups and bowls being stored inside bulk bins of rice.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REMOVE ALL CUPS AND BOWLS FROM BULK BINS. A SCOOP WITH A HANDLE CAN BE STORED INSIDE THE BULK BINS WITH ITS HANDLE STICKING UPWARDS. PLEASE MAKE THIS CORRECTION BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers of corn starch and garlic and large plastic jars were observed reused for the storage of dried spices, sauces, etc.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. MANUFACTURER CONTAINERS CANNOT BE REUSED TO STORE FOOD. PLEASE REMOVE ALL MANUFACTURER CONTAINERS OF CORN STARCH AND GARLIC, ETC. AND ANY OLD PLASTIC JARS AND USE NSF APPROVED CONTAINERS FOR THE STORAGE OF FOOD. PLEASE MAKE THIS CORRECTION BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION. THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.
